draft.title: The transactional model of stress
card: Lazarus and Folkman's transactional model says stress is not just the event itself. It depends on how a person judges the event and whether they believe they can cope.
the person judges what the event means for them. They may see it as irrelevant, positive, or stressful because it is a harm, a threat or a challenge.
the person judges whether they have the resources to cope, such as skills, time, money or support from others.
Stress is more likely when the event is seen as a threat and the person believes their resources are not enough. Two people can face the same event and respond differently.
draft.remember: Stress depends on the person's appraisal of the event and of their ability to cope.

a.q: In the transactional model, what does secondary appraisal involve?
opts: Judging whether one has the resources to cope
Judging whether an event is harmful or a threat
Reacting to an event with a rush of arousal
Using a strategy to deal with the stressor directly
a.why: Secondary appraisal is the judgement about coping resources, such as skills, time or support. Judging whether an event is a threat is primary appraisal, which is the tempting wrong option because it also happens early.
a.clue: Think about the person's own coping resources.

b.q: Two students in Geelong each get the same exam timetable. Priya thinks, "This is a chance to show what I know, and I have studied well." Sam thinks, "This will go badly and I have no one to help." Which best explains why Sam is more likely to feel stressed?
opts: Sam sees a threat and judges his resources as too low
Sam has a harder exam timetable than Priya has
Sam has a stronger fight or flight response than Priya
Sam avoids the exam while Priya approaches it
b.why: In the model, stress depends on appraisal, not only the event. Sam sees a threat and believes he lacks resources. The timetable is the same for both, so a harder exam cannot explain the difference.
b.clue: The event is the same for both students, so look at how each judges it.

a.best: Judging whether one has the resources to cope

b.best: Sam sees a threat and judges his resources as too low

The clue rules out the timetable option and says 'look at how each judges it'. The right option is the only one that uses 'judges', so the clue points straight to it.
